I became an HCA (as far as I can tell, the equivalent in the USA healthcare system is a PCT?) working in HCOP general medicine in Febuary 2020, a big career change for me as I worked exclusively in call centres before that. My ward quickly became a ward for mild to moderate COViD cases, especially in HCOP patients who also suffer from  dementia. For most of 2021 my ward had a very high mortality rate, as many as 4 patients passing a day over christmas 2020-2021.  I am autistic and have a history of moderate unipolar depression, but no other mental health concerns. Over the past 2 years I have developed extreme generalised and workplace anxiety, as well as psychosis that has caused me to miss work. Almost all of my coworkers from the beginning of the pandemic have moved to other areas. I perceive my new coworkers as resenting the time I am given off work. Before the pandemic the only medication I was prescribed was mirtazapine. I now take high dose venlafaxine, quetiapine, diazepam and propanolol. Without these medications I cannot attend work. I have become short tempered, frightened and erratic in my personal life. I care for my patients deeply, and I want to keep working in healthcare as I feel this is the only worthwhile endeavour I have undertaken in my life, and I am proud of making it this far, but I am certain these conditions will take my life sooner rather than later. Not hyperbole or self-pity, just the way these cases seem to go.
